name: Miles Roofing Playbook
label: Roofing
summary: Lead with full replacement plus financing; win storms with fast, honest inspections; never promise an insurance outcome. Use with the Miles Master Template (deploy logic, ZIP scoring, customer journey).

sections.title: Intro
lines: Lead with full replacement plus financing; win storms with fast, honest inspections; never promise an insurance outcome. Use with the Miles Master Template (deploy logic, ZIP scoring, customer journey).

sections.title: 1. At a glance
lines: Blended ticket ~$14,000; 35–45% gross margin; allowable cost per sold job 2,000
Flat/low-slope (rowhomes, urban) vs pitched shingle (suburban): separate ads, geo and landing pages

sections.title: 2. Seasonality by region
lines: Winter: leak repair, ice dams, retargeting; CPMs drop
Philly pattern: spring storms, summer steady, fall gold window
Pre-load storm budget each spring; inspection offer within days of hail
Hurricane prep, wind mitigation, post-storm tarping
Tile and foam/coatings; monsoon leak calls
Book dry-season installs early; moss and leak repair in winter
The core hail belt (TX, OK, KS, CO, NE, MO, IA) peaks March–August, heaviest April–June. About 40% of very large hail in 2022–2024 fell outside that region, so hail triggers run everywhere.

sections.title: 3. Location signals (add to ZIP score)
lines: Median year built and roof age: housing 15–25+ years old without a recent re-roof scores high.
Hail and wind event history (NOAA storm reports) in the last 1–3 years.
Owner-occupied single-family share; skip rental-heavy and condo ZIPs for retail replacement.
Housing stock: rowhome/flat-roof ZIPs get the flat-roof creative; suburban ZIPs get pitched shingle.
Affordability: ticket ÷ median income. Financing-first creative where the ratio is high.

sections.title: 4. Demographics and audiences
lines: Buyer: homeowner, typically 35–70, in the home 5+ years; older homeowners respond to warranty and trust, younger ones to financing and speed.
Meta: homeowners in scored ZIPs, Advantage+ audience; instant form set to Higher intent. Don't declare the Housing special ad category (roofing is a service).
Messaging: local crew, not a storm chaser; photos of the actual roof; honest "coating vs replacement" content.

Load with the Audience framework in the Master Template. Emergency segments get no income or homeowner filter and start at 25+; planned segments use the filters below. Ages are starting points: Miles tightens them from closed-won CRM data after 30 booked jobs.
median >= $70K: cash offer; $50-70K: financing-first; under $50K: skip prospecting
owner-occupied >= 60%; median year built <= 2005; single-family detached share high
Advantage+ on; control age 25, suggestion 35-65+; interests as suggestions: home improvement, roofing, home insurance
Search: replacement keywords; observe Homeowners, age 35+, HHI tiers; exclude Renters
ZIPs with hail >= 1 in. or wind >= 60 mph in last 7 days
Advantage+ on; geo = affected ZIPs only; control age 25
Search + LSA: storm/leak repair terms in affected ZIPs; no demographic exclusions
rowhome / attached housing share high; owner-occupied >= 50%
separate ad set and creative; same controls
separate ad group: flat roof, rubber roof, roof coating
Exclude in every segment: customers from the last 12 months (except retention campaigns), open leads and estimates, employees, out-of-area ZIPs.

sections.title: 5. Offer stack
lines: $500 off full replacement, booked by [date], + financing from $[X]/mo
Free gutter cleaning or guards with install; [X]-year workmanship warranty
Gutters, ventilation, skylights, impact-resistant (Class 4) shingles in hail ZIPs
Annual roof check; gutter cleaning coupon; storm re-inspection for past customers
Same-day leak repair / emergency tarp; no discount

sections.title: 6. Channels and campaign build
lines: Google Search: split replacement vs repair vs storm; negatives: DIY, jobs, materials, "shingle prices", unwanted roof types. LSA on.
Meta: 2 prospecting ad sets (flat vs pitched) on ABO + 1 retargeting campaign (social proof, price transparency, deadline). $20/day retargeting is enough to start.
CTA: Get Quote. Landing page: replacement-only, gallery, financing, warranty, certifications.
Budget lean: Search/LSA for repair and storm intent; Meta carries more weight for planned replacement than in other trades.

sections.title: 7. Triggers Miles watches
lines: Hail ≥ 1" or wind ≥ 60 mph reported in service ZIPs
Storm-inspection campaign in affected ZIPs within 24–48 hrs + SMS to past customers in those ZIPs
Shift to leak / ice dam repair
Pre-storm inspection, post-storm tarping and repair

sections.title: 8. After the job and retention
lines: Day 0: crew cleanup photos; thank-you coupon toward gutters or next service; honest review ask to everyone.
Day 7: referral offer with neighborhood photos (with permission): "recent work near [street]".
Month 11: annual roof check reminder. After any storm: free re-inspection text to past customers in hit ZIPs.

sections.title: 9. Compliance and watch-outs
lines: Never promise insurance will pay, waive deductibles, or act as a public adjuster unless licensed; many states regulate this.
Only claim scarcity and deadlines that are true; roofing buyers are suspicious and neighbors talk.
Financing language can trip Meta review; submit ads 24 hrs early.

sections.title: 10. Deploy checklist
lines: ☐ Confirm roof types installed (flat, shingle, metal, tile) and remove the rest from ads
☐ Score ZIPs; tag flat-roof vs pitched ZIPs; pull hail history
☐ Load offer stack with real financing terms and warranty years
☐ Build Search, LSA, Meta (2 prospecting + retargeting) and replacement landing page
☐ Arm hail/wind, freeze and storm triggers
☐ Turn on speed-to-lead, estimate follow-up, post-job, referral and storm re-inspection automations
☐ Get owner approval, launch, touch nothing days 1–3
Sources: hail season by state · hail outside Hail Alley (PropertyCasualty360 / Verisk) · economics from the Philadelphia $500-off roofing build.
